result:
Editing a response's reason phrase in the web UI now changes the flow's actual reason phrase. I haven't run any tests or the frontend build.

**Cause:** the UI sent the edit as `response.msg`. The `PUT /flows/<id>` handler in `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py` copied that onto `response.msg`, but `Response` has no `msg` attribute (it's called `reason`). So the handler just set an unused attribute, the real reason phrase never changed, and it went out unmodified.

**Changes:**
- `mitmproxy/tools/web/app.py`: the response update handler now accepts `reason` instead of `msg`, so the value lands on `Response.reason`.
- `web/src/js/components/FlowView/HttpMessages.tsx`: the reason phrase editor now sends `{ response: { reason } }`.
- `test/mitmproxy/tools/web/test_app.py`: the PUT test now sends `reason` and asserts `f.response.reason`. Before, it checked `f.response.msg`, which passed only because of the stray attribute.

The handler no longer accepts `msg`, so any external client that was sending it will need to switch to `reason`. The response JSON the UI reads already used `reason`, so nothing changed there.
